domain::tddd::type_signals_doc::construc.docs: Domain-owned construction seam that passes one immutable rustdoc JSON byte slice to the adapter-supplied decoder and derives the content hash from that same slice, yielding CapturedRustdocJson without placing JSON parsing behavior on the value object.

Domain-owned identity-bearing construction seam that binds one RustdocExecutionIdentity to the content hash and typed decode produced from the exact same immutable byte slice in a single call; RustdocCrateAdapter supplies the decoder and calls this function inside the trusted-root lock interval rather than pairing an identity with an independently constructed capture.

domain::tddd::type_signals_doc::decide_t.docs: Returns SkipEvaluation only when the verified complete cache keys are equal; every mismatch requires fresh rustdoc extraction and evaluation, with no partial-snapshot reuse.

CatalogueToExtendedCratePort.docs: Accept the complete same-track catalogue set and a LayerId-keyed authoritative rustdoc context for every TDDD layer so external add placement follows the declaring layer (GO-01, IN-01, IN-02, CO-01, CO-02, CO-03, AC-01, AC-02, AC-03).

RustdocCratePort.docs: Synchronous blocking-I/O secondary port and the sole public construction boundary for captured rustdoc values. Baseline loading decodes and hashes one immutable byte vector into CapturedRustdocJson without claiming a current execution identity. capture_current constructs RustdocSnapshot as one identity-bearing capture proof inside the same trusted-root lock interval; callers cannot assemble a snapshot from independently constructed identity and JSON values. Both complete on the caller thread; timeout, unsupported platform, untrusted roots, and non-authoritative outputs fail without retry or fallback.

methods.docs: Synchronous baseline-only filesystem and decoding boundary: read one frozen baseline path on the caller thread, hash and typed-decode the same immutable bytes inside the infrastructure adapter, and return the opaque CapturedRustdocJson value. It deliberately carries no RustdocExecutionIdentity because baseline loading does not claim a current Cargo export identity; no internal async scheduling is provided.
methods.name: load_from_path

methods.docs: Synchronous blocking export and construction boundary: resolve and validate the complete execution identity, acquire the trusted-root lock, wait for at most 120 seconds, run rustdoc export, verify the expected output, hash and typed-decode its immutable bytes, and construct one identity-bearing RustdocSnapshot before returning on the caller thread. No independently supplied identity/capture pair, internal async scheduling, retry, or lockless fallback is accepted.
methods.name: capture_current

SchemaExporter.docs: Baseline-identical secondary port for extracting a crate's public API schema; carried so RustdocSchemaExporter trait-implementation edges remain explicit.

AuthoritativeRustdocContext.docs: Value-equatable authoritative context carrying its validated LayerId, baseline crate, and immutable locked current rustdoc snapshot; evaluation reads this captured generation only and never re-reads paths.

CapturedRustdocJson.docs: Opaque validated content-addressed value supplied only by the infrastructure RustdocCratePort boundary after one immutable rustdoc JSON byte vector has produced both its RustdocJsonHash and parsed rustdoc_types::Crate. The domain value exposes no byte-decoding constructor and never receives raw serialized input.

CargoProfileName.docs: Validated non-empty Cargo profile selected for one rustdoc export and included in its reuse identity.

ExpectedRustdocJsonPath.docs: Validated expected rustdoc JSON path confined to the resolved Cargo target directory and bound into the cache identity.

ImplementationFingerprint.docs: Content identity of the complete bounded workspace rustdoc input set and the exact D3 environment allowlist; unavailable external inputs, symlinks, I/O races, or any D4 limit violation produce no value.

ResolutionFingerprint.docs: Content identity of architecture rules and the complete configured catalogue and rustdoc-baseline byte sets captured from one authoritative resolution snapshot.

ResolvedCargoTargetDirectory.docs: Resolved absolute Cargo target directory value. It validates only absoluteness and deliberately carries no trusted-root or no-follow admission claim; RustdocCrateAdapter solely enforces Unix descriptor-relative no-follow validation, including every parent of an explicitly external target, before capture.

RustdocExecutionIdentity.docs: Value-equatable selection of the resolved absolute Cargo target directory, crate, validated feature set, profile, and expected rustdoc JSON path used for one export. Construction validates that the expected JSON path is contained by the selected target directory; trusted-root admission remains solely owned by RustdocCrateAdapter when it creates the capture proof.

RustdocExecutionIdentityError.docs: Failure to construct a complete rustdoc execution identity from a resolved absolute target path, contained expected output, and non-empty profile. Trusted-root admission failures belong to RustdocCratePortError because only RustdocCrateAdapter performs that check.

RustdocJsonHash.docs: Content identity of the exact rustdoc JSON bytes read while the matching target-directory lock remains held.

RustdocSnapshot.docs: Opaque identity-bearing capture proof supplied only by RustdocCratePort::capture_current after RustdocCrateAdapter validates the identity's target root and derives the exact JSON-byte hash and parsed crate inside one lock interval. It has no public constructor from separate RustdocExecutionIdentity and CapturedRustdocJson values, so mixed-generation assembly is not part of the contract and paths are never re-read for equality.

domain::tddd::type_signals_doc::TypeSign.docs: Complete reuse identity binding declaration, baseline, HEAD, implementation and resolution fingerprints, and the exact Cargo/rustdoc execution selection; every component must match on a clean worktree.
Persisted type-signals result whose cache key carries the complete D3 execution and input identity and is replaced only after final fingerprint revalidation.
Closed reuse outcome: either every identity matches and evaluation is skipped, or rustdoc is re-extracted and evaluated without partial reuse.
Opaque verified pair of recorded and current complete cache keys constructible only for a clean worktree and readable authority snapshot.
